items.note: Grant traces Paramāra genealogy: Sindhurāja, Bhōjadēva, Udayāditya, Naravarman, identical with the previous grant.
Naravarman donated twenty nivartanas of land, measured by a daṇḍa of ninety-six parvas, on the 12th of bright Māgha 1162 (3 February 1110 A.C.).
Earlier grants of twenty halas: ten by Mahāmaṇḍalīka Rājyadēva (VS 1154), four by his wife, six by Naravarman (VS 1159).
Gift lands lay in the western Betwā valley; the Chandēlla king's success against the Mālavas is cited, and the Betwā region was a bone of contest between Paramāras and Chandēllas.
refs: Ajayagadh rock inscription of Vivavarman, VS 1317

items.note: Madanavarman's Augasī plate of VS 1190 (1133 A.D.) gives a gift from Bhillasvāimpura (modern Bhilsā); Naravarman struggled with enemies across the Bētwā, the Chaulukyas and the Chāhamāna Abhayadeva.
Banerji linked the Upēndrapura-maṇḍala with a town in the Rāṇḍod inscription; editor places it in the south-eastern Shivpurī District just west of the Bētwā, around Rāṇḍ.

items.note: The inscribed pillar stands in the Bijā Mandir at Vidishā, originally a Hindu temple and later converted into a mosque.
26 lines, mostly well preserved, 63 by 16 cm; characters Nāgarī of the twelfth century, letters 2 to 2.5 cm.
Vidishā record expresses devotion to Chachchikā/Charchikā, favourite goddess of Naravarman alias Nirvāṇa-Nārāyaṇa; undated but assigned to his reign (1094-1133 A.C. per text).
The pillar belongs to a temple of Chachchikā, which may have been built by Naravarman alias Nirvāṇa-Nārāyaṇa in devotion to the deity.

items.note: Sircar concluded that the Sun-god eulogy slab, found at Bhilsā (Vidishā), belonged to the temple of Bhāilla-svāmin.
The name Bhilsā still retains the memory of the Sun-deity, to whom a temple existed there some time back.
The Vidishā Sun-god eulogy is called significant in the history of Sanskrit literature, by a mahākavi-chakravartin named Chhittapa.
Characters are Nāgarī of about the eleventh century A.C.
